Comrades 2023 - No Comradeship

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What was billed as a historic Comrades Marathon turned out to be anticlimactic for many in SA's vast running community...As many runners were cut off before reaching the finish line,with many saying t

Unique Selling Point:
I wanted to highlight to you that there was an issue at the Comrades marathon this year that unfairly cost approximately 800-900 runners a medal. There were no runners on the finish line when the gun went off at 12 hours, which actually defeats the purpose of the race. Many people tune in for the last couple of minutes to see the last runners over the finish line. Yet this year the field was empty. I was one of them. I got cut off at the last cut-off which was approx. 6.3km left with an hour to spare. I was averaging 8.02mins per km at that stage. If you do the math I could have finished even if I walked. But I was not afforded the opportunity to attempt a probable finish. I would also like to add I have finished 10 consecutive Comrades marathons all between 11- 12 hours and 2023 is the first year I got cut off. The Comrades is a huge event under the running community. The entry fees have become excessive. Hours of training go into prepping, and not to mention the amount of money to go to races in preparation for the race etc. There is some scepticism amongst some very well-known coaches that the Comrades Marathon Association will not take the time of day to respond to the field of runners that were impacted to explain why the cut-offs were made stricter this year which in essence cost so many runners their medals. This is arrogance is what is the issue to me. At least just explain to us what was the logic to decrease the last cut-off time with 10 mins from the last year. If you do decide to look into this story you will also find other issues relating to the start of the race, bottlenecks on the road etc. One very positive thing is Gerda Steyn breaking the long-standing record of Frith van Der Merwe which I think is for sure something to highlight too. The Running Man has done a blog on Facebook on this issue and released some stats.

Script : Comrades
[0pening music fades in]

1.V/O : Every day as the first rays of the sun paint the horizon, the sound of footsteps echoes through the streets.
Upsound Vanessa Briglal :38:12 There's something about being on the road with no one around you, the peace and tranquillity. And what your body is capable of astounds you.
2.V/O Across the country runners test their physical and mental endurance …each step bringing them closer to their ultimate test. [breather,transition]

3.V/O Each year thousands of runners take on this Iconic 89-kilometre ultramarathon, weaving through rolling hills between Pietermaritzburg and Durban.
4.V/O With a 102-year history, the Comrades draws elite athletes and novices alike…and the spectators who watch breathlessly as runners push their bodies to the limit. [breather]
Link : For many, the Comrades Marathon is not just a race, it’s a symbol of human spirit and comradery (camaraderie). It all culminates in a single moment …Crossing the finish line. [breather, Vanessa running, breathing ]
VO: But this year, for hundreds of would-be finishers, something went wrong. [foreboding]
[breather with Vanessa running]
5.V/ O Reasons for taking on the Comrades are as diverse as the participants themselves, but for 53-year-old Vanessa Briglal, this year's race had a special significance.
Upsound Vanessa Briglal:03:07 The last comrades I ran was in 2019 and that was the year that I lost my husband.[breather]
Upsound Vanessa Briglal 03:26 He was my greatest supporter.
Upsound Vanessa Briglal :03:43 So when Comrades released the date late last year, that the marathon was going to fall on the 11th of June, I knew without a doubt that I had to get the start because the 11th of June would have been our wedding anniversary.
6.V/O With only six months to prepare Vanessa was determined to make it to the starting line…relentlessly hitting the road for 3 hours every morning.
Upsound Vanessa Briglal : 04:57 I was at the peak of my fitness. [pause] And I got to the start on the 11th of June, 05:25And it's always incredible, you know, it's dark, you lean on each other. And the emotions, they just well up.
[ breather Comrades start anticipation, Nat sound]
[Start of the race, pistol]
Upsound Vanessa :05:37And I had my pacing plan. I had planned that I would beat each cutoff by 10 minutes.//
VO: Race organizers divide the Comrades course into five sections, allocating each one a cut-off: a maximum time in which runners must run that section, if they are to finish the race within the 12-hour limit.
[ Cut off visuals]
Upsound Vanessa :05:37 // I had no challenges getting through each cutoff. [breath]
8.V/O Approaching the penultimate cut-off point, Vanessa’s official Comrades Marathon runners app, which tracked her average pace, had her comfortably making it. [ visuals of her Comrades app screenshot sent to you]
Upsound Vanessa 07:06 I could see it in front of me. And the official raised his hand and shot off the gun as we came to the cutoff. We should have had 10 minutes more till 3 p.m. but the gun went off at 2.50.
9.V/O Vanessa was one of hundreds of runners left bewildered - cut off before the finish line even though they believed they were on track to finish the race.
Upsound Vanessa 07:34 I have run comrades before but I've never been cut off. It was surreal. This shouldn't be happening but there were broken people at that cutoff.
Stuart : So this is the Sherwood cut off, you can see the clock over there, so listen for the gun there is the gun. 55 on the clock, so they fired the gun 5-6 seconds early. These runners are cut off.
Lourensa : They could have made it. They should have made it!
10.V/O Stuart Mann is a running enthusiast who blogs as the Running Man. He believes many runners were denied their hard-earned finishes thanks to oversights by race management.
[Stuart demo segment]
Upsound Stuart01:34 Added to the confusion was that the official Comrades app...02:03actually had last year's cut-offs, so they had incorrect times which showed you did have the extra 10 minutes. [...] they thought they had plenty of time.
[Transition]
VO: In past years, runners have had 12 hours to complete the Marathon, but this year, that time was reduced by ten minutes - meaning runners had even LESS time to reach each cut-off than they thought.
Upsound Stuart Mann :00:53 [...] So it's almost like double taxation. And runners did communicate this, but they were ignored.//So yeah, about 600 people who should have got a medal this year would have been denied a medal.
Bruce Fordyce 0:24 the finish is the highlight. When the gun goes up. That's the dramatic moment. People coming around the final bend, trying desperately to make it, helping each other…
[ final cut off Comrades 2023]
VO: Comrades Legend Bruce Fordyce was commentating on the race from the SuperSport studio. After South African Gerda Steyn broke the women’s record, he looked forward to the drama of the race’s final moments…but the field was empty. The last runners had already been swept off the route.
Upsound Bruce Fordyce0:54 it was almost like trying to talk about a vacuum. There was nothing to talk about. Whereas normally you've got, I don't know, Joe Dlamini from Soweto struggling as hard as he can to get there and Mr. Smith from Cape Town, can he make it, can he make it? Nothing, it was just nothing.
13 V/O So what was really going on? We spoke to Race Director Rowyn James.
[Zoom interview rake two] Lorensa 05:21 Okay, Rowan, can you explain to us the rationale and the thinking behind the new cutoffs?
ROWAN 09:19 there's pressure on us as event organizers to open the N3 highway in particular, which is a national logistics route from Durban up to Johannesburg.
VO: But, says Mann, this doesn’t make sense.
Upsound Stuart O4:02 it doesn't really hold water because the roads are closed for most of the day. An extra 10 minutes for a race that starts at 5 -30 in the morning?
09:48
secondly, also from a medical perspective, point of view as well is that we, we as event organizers have got to ensure that we have, I mean, present a safe, secure race for the participants as well. So the last thing that you want to do is potentially get into a situation where you're setting unrealistic times or targets that then people get into some sort of medical distress as well.
[ Take one Zoom interview] Lourensa questio Official Comrades app still had the previous cut-offs, and that caused a lot of confusion.
[ Take one Zoom interview] Roweyn James 24:49 : Yes, I am aware that the app wasn't updated. I can only apologize for that. It's water under the bridge. I think the important thing that learning for us is to take the feedback that we've received to ensure that in future years, that to check the app.
14 :V/O This is little consolation for runners like Vanessa. Who believe the Comrades as more than just a race, but a symbol of the unwavering human spirit
Upsound Vanessa Briglal : 10:21 That opportunity will never come back. There will never be another 11th of June comrades anytime soon. This was the moment. The reassurance I have is that I know I would have finished the race [ running shot ]
